rationale: The buyer is real — an indie dev already spending $200/month — and the pain (budget evaporating mid-workflow) is frequent and significant. However, the solution (an LLM cost-routing proxy or managed self-hosted open model tuned for computer-use) requires non-trivial infrastructure: model hosting, GPU compute procurement, latency-sensitive API proxying, and ongoing model benchmarking to maintain the '80% capability' promise. None of that is buildable as a Claude prompt + Stripe link by a solo non-technical operator, and each customer interaction (onboarding credentials, tuning, support for model drift) demands per-customer human work. The total falls below the 5.5 validate threshold, and even if it cleared that, buildability (3) and operational_autonomy (3) both fail their build gates badly.
solution_plan: This opportunity is not viable for a solo non-technical operator running a Claude-based factory. The core product is infrastructure: either a GPU-backed self-hosted LLM cluster or a smart API routing layer that benchmarks open models against frontier ones. Building, maintaining, and reliably delivering that requires engineering expertise and cloud infrastructure management well beyond Claude prompts + a landing page + Stripe. A solo operator could not build or maintain this without becoming a full-time DevOps/MLOps practitioner. Pass on this one.
notes: Fails buildability_with_ai (3 < 6 min) and operational_autonomy (3 < 7 min) build gates. Total 4.9 is also below the 5.5 validate threshold — drop.
